note: Two things set Arkansas apart. Its child abuse hotline is run by the State Police Crimes Against Children Division rather than by the human services department, so a report there goes straight to law enforcement. And the Office of Long-Term Care - the sole licensing authority for Psychiatric Residential Treatment Facilities - now publishes its monitoring reports, complaint visit reports, corrective action plans and notices of adverse action online, so you can read a facility's record before you call.

channels.name: Arkansas Board of Examiners in Counseling and Marriage and Family Therapy
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes complaints against its licensees and applicants from any person, investigates them and disciplines licences.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed professional counselor or marriage and family therapist in Arkansas.
channels.how: Complaints must be in writing and on the Board's own complaint form, which is filed through its online portal.
channels.mail: Arkansas Board of Examiners in Counseling, Freeway Medical Center, 5800 W. 10th Street, Suite 405, Little Rock, AR 72204

channels.name: Arkansas Psychology Board
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes complaints about the practice of any of its licensees, from any concerned citizen or organisation, and disciplines licences.
channels.how: The complaint must be in writing, and the document has to be signed and dated. It goes to the Board's Complaints Committee.
channels.mail: Arkansas Psychology Board, Complaints Committee, 101 East Capitol, Suite 415, Little Rock, AR 72201

channels.name: Arkansas Social Work Licensing Board
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines social workers in Arkansas.
channels.how: Contact the Board for its complaint form.

channels.name: Arkansas Office of Long-Term Care (Psychiatric Residential Treatment Facilities)
channels.what_it_can_do: The sole licensing authority for Psychiatric Residential Treatment Facilities in Arkansas. It licenses, surveys, regulates and investigates them, and takes enforcement action against failed facility practices.
channels.who_to_report: A PRTF - the licensed psychiatric residential category most Arkansas programs in this industry fall under.
channels.how: Call the complaint hotline or email the complaints address.
channels.note: Arkansas publishes PRTF monitoring and complaint visit reports, corrective action plans and notices of adverse action online. Read what has already been found against a program before you file.

channels.name: Arkansas Child Abuse Hotline (State Police Crimes Against Children Division)
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line for child maltreatment, run by the Arkansas State Police rather than by the human services department, so a report reaches law enforcement directly.
channels.who_to_report: A child at an Arkansas program. Anyone may report, at any hour.
channels.how: Call. Have the child's name and address, the alleged offender's name and address, and what happened. If a child's life may be in immediate danger, call 911 or local law enforcement first, then the hotline. Mandated reporters can file through the secure online portal instead.
channels.phone_note: Also 1-844-SAVE-A-CHILD. 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

channels.name: Disability Rights Arkansas
channels.what_it_can_do: Arkansas's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: An Arkansas program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
